entries.name: Cable Row
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing was against this text: it showed a chair-height seat with the cable coming up from the floor. Source-bound side-view draft: sitting tall at a low row station with the feet planted on the plate and the handle in long arms toward the low pulley; the trunk does not rock while the elbows drive down and back and the handle comes to the lower ribs, then a slower return to long arms. The cable only lengthens on the pull. Not drawn: the shoulder blades reaching forward at the end of the return.
entries.summary: Sitting tall at the cable row with the feet planted, drive the elbows toward the back pockets from long arms, then return slowly without the torso rocking.

frames.caption: Sit at the cable row with the feet planted and the handle held in long arms.
Drive the elbows toward the back pockets.
Keep the torso tall and quiet.
Return slowly, reaching the shoulder blades forward.
If the torso rocks, reduce the load before shortening the reach.

entries.name: Band Row
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: standing tall with the band running from a chest-height anchor to both hands; the hands travel from a long reach toward the ribs with the elbows leading back, and the band visibly stretches through the pull. No database media row exists under this name; the standard chest-height anchor was drawn (listed in the daily review). The hands now reach the body: the torso is the vertical line at x 44.5, and the pulling position comes to within 3.0 of it, against 8.5 before, so the frames named for reaching the ribs and the neck now actually do. The elbow is solved on the shoulder circle from the authored hand, so the upper arm (12.5) and forearm (12.0) hold their length by construction. Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Six drawn positions of a band row, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Start with both arms reaching long toward the anchor.
Drive the elbows behind you to start the pull.
Elbows past the ribs; the upper back finishes.
Pause with the torso tall and quiet.
Return the reach slowly.
Full reach again, tension still on the band.

entries.name: Cable Rope Rear-Delt Rows
entries.reason: Own drawn frames authored for this repository: seated tall at a low cable with the rope reaching forward at shoulder height; the pull drives the elbows wide and back to the upper chest, the rope ends separating at the finish. No database media row exists under this name; the standard low-cable rope setup was drawn (listed in the daily review). Draft preview pending qualified technique review.
entries.summary: Eight drawn positions of a cable rope rear-delt row, seen from the side.

frames.caption: Reach forward at shoulder height with the rope held in both hands.
Drive the elbows wide toward the back wall.
Keep the elbows wide through the finish.
Rope at the upper chest; the rear shoulders finish.
Pause with the torso tall and quiet.
Return wide along the same path.
Reach the shoulder blades forward again.
Full reach again at shoulder height.

entries.name: Low Pulley Row To Neck
entries.reason: Redrawn on 8 October 2026 at the owner's request, because the earlier drawing contradicted this text: it showed the athlete standing. Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 55 degrees so the wide elbows show: sitting at a low row station with the back upright, the feet on the plate and the knees slightly bent, arms straight toward the low pulley; the elbows lift high and wide and the rope comes to the neck until the hands are beside the ears and the upper arms are level, a pause, and a slower return to straight arms. The trunk and legs do not move. Not drawn: the palms-down grip.
entries.summary: Seated at a low cable row with the back upright, lift the elbows high and wide to pull the rope to the neck, hands beside the ears, pause, then return slowly to straight arms.

frames.caption: Sit at a low cable row station holding the rope ends with the palms facing down, back upright, knees slightly bent and arms straight in front.
Keeping the torso still, lift the elbows and pull the rope toward the neck until the hands are beside the ears and the upper arms are level with the floor.
Pause. Elbows high and wide.
Return slowly until the arms are straight.
Torso stays upright and still.

entries.name: Shotgun Row
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, from the description accepted that day: the earlier drawing showed an upright two-handed row to the chest. Source-bound side-view draft: a wide split stance leaning forward from the hips with a flat back, the leg opposite the working arm in front and the free hand on its thigh; the near arm reaches straight down the cable's line to a low pulley, then rows the handle to the side of the lower ribs with the elbow passing behind the body, pauses, and returns. The trunk and legs do not move. The cable only lengthens on the pull. One side is shown; the last caption carries the change of sides. Not drawn: the palm turning up.
entries.summary: In a wide split stance leaning forward with a flat back, row a single handle from a low cable to the side of your lower ribs, pause, return under control, then change sides.

frames.caption: Clip a single handle to a low pulley and face it in a wide split stance with the leg opposite the working arm in front; lean forward from the hips with a flat back, rest the free hand on the front thigh, and hold the handle with the arm straight.
Draw the shoulder blade back and bend the elbow to row the handle to the side of your lower ribs, turning the palm up as you pull.
Pause briefly. Lean forward, back flat, no twisting.
Return under control to the reach.
Complete the repetitions and change sides.

entries.name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
techniqueCitations: Haff, G. G., & Triplett, N. T. (Eds.). (2016). Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.). Human Kinetics, pp. 396-397.
McGill, S. M. (2014). Ultimate Back Fitness and Performance (5th ed.). Backfitpro Inc., pp. 210-214.
entries.reason: Authored coordinate prototype with canonical 11-joint topology, horizontal bench support, and.

frames.caption: Let the working arm reach long while the trunk stays braced and still.
Drive the elbow toward the hip, then lower to the full reach.
Cue: Drive the elbow toward the hip. Keep the torso square.
Lower smoothly back toward full reach.
If the torso rotates, reduce the load before shortening the row.

entries.summary: Five drawn positions of a single-arm dumbbell row, seen from the side.

entries.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
entries.reason: Redrawn on 9 October 2026 at the owner's request, from the description accepted that day: the earlier drawing was borrowed from Single-Arm Dumbbell Row, which finishes with the elbow toward the hip, where this text finishes beside the chest. Source-bound side-view draft with its own drawing: one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench, the other foot flat on the floor and the trunk level; the dumbbell hangs on a straight arm under the shoulder and is pulled up beside the chest with the elbow rising past the back, a short squeeze, and a slower lowering to a long arm. The trunk and legs do not move. The dumbbell is held end-on to the viewer's line, as a palm facing in holds it. One side is shown; the last caption carries the change of sides.
entries.summary: With one knee and the same-side hand on a bench and the torso level, pull the dumbbell from a long arm up to the side of the chest, squeeze, lower it straight down, then change sides.

frames.caption: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench with the other foot flat on the floor, and bend forward until your torso is level with the floor and your back is flat, holding a dumbbell in the free hand, palm facing in, with the arm hanging straight.
Keeping the torso still and the upper arm close to your side, pull the dumbbell straight up to the side of the chest.
Squeeze the back. Flat back, torso still.
Lower it straight down to a long arm.
Complete the repetitions, then change sides.
